subject: Geography
central_question: How does atmospheric moisture move through evaporation, humidity, condensation, clouds, precipitation, rainfall types, and global rainfall distribution?
in_scope_units: Water vapour, atmospheric moisture, absolute humidity, relative humidity, saturation, and dew point.
Evaporation, transpiration, latent heat, and controls of evaporation.
Dew, frost, fog, mist, smog, and clouds.
Cloud types and combinations by height and vertical development.
Precipitation as rain, snow, sleet, and hail.
World distribution and seasonal effectiveness of rainfall.

known_pitfalls.claim: Relative humidity is the actual mass of water vapour per unit volume.
known_pitfalls.correction: That is absolute humidity; relative humidity compares present moisture with the air’s capacity at the same temperature.

known_pitfalls.claim: Dew and frost form under identical temperature conditions.
known_pitfalls.correction: Dew forms when the dew point is above freezing, while frost forms when condensation or deposition occurs at or below freezing.

known_pitfalls.claim: Fog and cloud are completely unrelated.
known_pitfalls.correction: Fog is essentially a cloud with its base at or near the ground.

known_pitfalls.claim: The windward and leeward sides receive equal orographic rainfall.
known_pitfalls.correction: Rising windward air cools and rains; descending leeward air warms and produces a rain shadow.
Precipitation includes rain, snow, sleet, and hail.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1(ii): identify evaporation as liquid-to-vapour transformation.
NCERT Exercise 2(iv): explain and classify clouds.
NCERT Exercise 3(ii): compare condensation forms and dew–frost formation.
NCERT Exercise 3(i): explain world precipitation patterns.
